what: Aon is a global professional services firm centred on insurance broking. It places insurance and reinsurance, advises on risk and pensions, and since buying NFP serves mid-sized US companies as well as large ones.
customers: Large corporations, insurers needing reinsurance, and mid-market companies through NFP.
money: commercial risk broking and reinsurance broking
health benefits, pensions and workforce consulting
moat: Analytics and claims data across whole industries that help clients negotiate, and relationships with the world's largest insurance buyers.
risks: Debt rose to about $29 billion after the NFP acquisition
Commission income softens when insurance pricing falls
Consulting demand weakens in a downturn
Integrating NFP's many small offices takes time
opportunities: Revenue is recurring because policies renew every year
NFP opens the mid-market, a larger and faster-growing segment than large corporates
It takes no underwriting risk, so margins are steadier than an insurer's
watch: Organic revenue growth and free cash flow against debt reduction.
